A banner names the account, lists the positions, says plainly they were not taken over — no take profit, no stop, no ladder — and offers Turn on the Manual Bot & manage them or Leave them alone . Neither is a default, and choosing to leave them means exactly that.

sections.title: 🧮 Start to finish, with real numbers
sections.text: 🧮 Start to finish, with real numbers One position opened by hand, from the click on the exchange to the exit, with every figure worked from the settings named. The setup Manual Bot, running, Direction Both , Pairs All pairs . DCA: size type Dollar, First DCA 100 , Deviation 5% , Orders 3 , Volume scale 2 , Step scale 2 , Orders on exchange 3 . Exits: Take profit type Percentage from average price , Take profit 1% , Stop loss 20% , SL offset from Initial entry price . 1 · You open the trade yourself On the exchange, by hand: SOLUSDT long, 5 SOL at 200.00 — 1,000 USDT of position, at whatever leverage you chose. The app had nothing to do with it. 2 · About a second later, it is picked up The exchange pushes a private message; the app re-reads the account, finds a position no bot here opened, no other bot claims the pair, and your scope allows it. You get: "picked up the SOLUSDT long (5 @ 200) you opened yourself — it is placing the DCA ladder, take profit and stop loss now." 3 · What it puts on the venue The ladder is measured from 200.00, the average your position had at pickup. Distances accumulate ×2: 5%, then 5+10 = 15%, then 15+20 = 35%. Sizes multiply ×2: 100, 200, 400. DCA 1  ·  −5%  ·  buy 100 USDT  @  190.00 DCA 2  ·  −15%  ·  buy 200 USDT  @  170.00 DCA 3  ·  −35%  ·  buy 400 USDT  @  130.00 TP  ·  +1%  ·  sell 5 SOL  @  202.00 SL  ·  −20% from 200.00  ·  watched at 160.00 (no order on the venue) All three ladder steps rest at once, because "Orders on exchange" is 3. A second message follows: "is now managing SOLUSDT — its take profit is resting on the exchange and the DCA ladder is in place." Now it is protected. 4 · Price falls to 190.00 and the first step fills 100 USDT buys 100 ÷ 190 = 0.5263 SOL . size    5.0000 + 0.5263 = 5.5263 SOL spent   1,000 + 100    = 1,100 USDT average 1,100 ÷ 5.5263  = 199.05 Your average moved from 200.00 to 199.05 and the exit came with it, from 202.00 to 201.04 — about half a percent nearer to where price actually is. That is the trade DCA makes for you: a closer exit, bought with 100 USDT more on the position. 5 · What moves, and what does not The take profit re-anchors. The order at 202.00 for 5 SOL is cancelled and replaced at 199.05 × 1.01 = 201.04 for 5.5263 SOL — both price and quantity had to change. The remaining ladder steps do not move. DCA 2 still rests at 170.00 and DCA 3 at 130.00, measured from 200.00 as they always were; the fill above them does not drag them up. The stop does not move either, on "Initial entry price": still 160.00. On "Current entry price (avg)" it would have walked to 199.05 × 0.80 = 159.24. 6 · Price recovers and the take profit fills The reduce-only limit at 201.04 fills for the whole 5.5263 SOL. At 1% above the average, the gross result is 1% of what is on the trade: 1,100 × 0.01 = +11.00 USDT before fees. The app books the exact fill price, not the target. 7 · Cleaning up The unfilled ladder orders at 170.00 and 130.00 are cancelled. Could either not be confirmed cancelled, the app would keep the pair and say CLEANUP BLOCKED . The stop stops being watched, the deal leaves "Managing now", and the trade is recorded under the Manual Bot's P&L. The pair is released, and the next SOLUSDT trade starts the sequence from scratch. The same trade, if it had kept falling. With the stop off, all three steps fill at 190.00, 170.00 and 130.00 — 1,000 + 100 + 200 + 400 = 1,700 USDT on a trade you opened as a 1,000 USDT position, at an average of 173.83 . One fast wick can do all three inside a single candle, because levels fill on touch. Now put the stop back. At 160.00 it sits above the deepest step at 130.00, so price reaches it after the second fill and the deal closes at market: the third step never fills and the loss is booked on 1,300 USDT at an average of 193.95 — about 228 USDT , well beyond the 20% of your original 1,000 the setting looks like it promises, because the ladder added 300 USDT on the way down. A stop inside your own ladder ends the deal before the ladder has finished its job, and what it risks is not the number you typed.
